provenance.paper_title: HAM-VLN: Harnessing Hierarchical Agentic Memory for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation

evidence.paraphrase: Recent depth-grounded waypoints remain verbatim within a bounded window.

representation_paths.memory_component: persistent world graph and reflection notes

evidence.paraphrase: The agent records room, object, progress, and failure information in a depth-grounded graph.
Each action decision also writes semantic and reflective information into the world graph. For HAM-VLN, this specifically supports fixed-rule insertion or replacement of recent waypoint observations.
Older verbatim waypoints leave the bounded recent window. For HAM-VLN, this specifically supports explicit deletion or eviction of stored items of recent waypoint observations.

Older history is re-accessed by relevance, recency, salience, and one-hop graph expansion. For HAM-VLN, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of recent waypoint observations.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 2): During inference, the operative memory component (recent waypoint observations) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, explicit deletion or eviction of stored items, relinking or reindexing of stored items; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
